title: Cora convicts
goal: As Cora, I want concrete duplicity to place the checkpoint into pending termination custody, receive the conviction bond, and enable a later consuming fold to retire the registry key.

steps.say: Alice lands her first rotation. Its prior-next commitment anchors both branches of the later duplicity proof.
Alice has poisoned the epoch (Mallory has the keys). A conviction does not care which state the checkpoint is in.

Cora supplies a conflicting rotation at sequence 1. Both branches satisfy the common prior-next commitment and their signing and derived-witness thresholds. Cora holds a commitment naming this key state, this evidence and herself, opened by a transaction whose validity range ended in the slot before; the poison that landed since leaves it as it was, and the conviction reveals it. The checkpoint enters termination-pending custody, keeping its token and key state. D goes to Cora; B and the pool return to the refund address. The registry key remains active until the later consuming fold.
Without a second receipted rotation at the tip’s sequence there is no conviction.
Pending termination custody refuses a local rotation.
Pending termination custody refuses a top-up.

forks.title: Inception is not an ordinary rotation

steps.say: A sequence-zero sibling cannot be later than its prior establishment. The concrete rotation predicate refuses this evidence.
Mallory sees Cora’s evidence and submits the same conviction paying herself. The only commitment over this output and this evidence names Cora, so the conviction is refused.

forks.title: A commitment opened in the conviction’s slot

steps.say: A commitment whose opening transaction is valid up to this very slot is not yet eligible: whoever sees the evidence first cannot open a commitment and convict in one block.
Before Cora’s conviction lands, someone tops up the pool. The top-up changes the pool; the key state Cora’s commitment names stays.
Cora’s commitment names the key state, not the output the top-up spent: her conviction is accepted and D goes to her. The refund address receives B and the pool, top-up included.
Before Cora’s conviction lands, Alice rotates to sequence 2. Only the holder of the next keys can do this. The checkpoint now carries another key state.

Cora’s commitment names the key state before the rotation. Even with a proof against the new key state on the table, it entitles nothing now: her conviction is refused. A conviction of the new key state needs a commitment that names it.
